description: Suresh's alibi (WS-2: in Bengaluru until 11pm on 19 March) directly conflicts with CCTV placing his vehicle on the Tumakuru highway at 9:40pm the same night - a ~90min drive that makes both being-in-Bengaluru-until-11pm AND being-on-the-highway-at-9:40pm mutually exclusive.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Suresh to account for his vehicle's presence on NH-48 at 9:40pm on 19 March, given his statement places him in Rajajinagar until 11pm the same night.

description: Ravindra's statement (WS-2) denies ever dealing with Praveen, but CCTV (CC-2) places Praveen entering his shop the morning after the robbery, and a planning call (CL-1) precedes the robbery by 4 days.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Ravindra to explain the 20 Feb 4-day-prior call to Praveen and the CCTV footage of Praveen entering his shop the morning after the robbery, given his statement he's never dealt with him.

description: Tarun's statement (WS-2) claims QuickCash and RapidFin are unrelated companies he had no connection to besides RapidFin - but both companies' payouts (TX-1, TX-2) land in the exact same Kotak account belonging to Zoya, and his own recurring call pattern to her (CL-1, CL-2, CL-3) spans both FIRs' complaint windows without a gap.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Tarun why 'unrelated' QuickCash and RapidFin payouts both settle into the same Kotak xx3390 account, and why his weekly ops calls to that account's holder don't stop between the two companies' operating windows.

description: Notary Shantaram's statement (WS-1) claims he doesn't know the buyer personally, but a call record (CL-3) shows him speaking directly with the buyer, and he received a payment from the broker (TX-2) the day after the buyer's payment cleared - inconsistent with an arm's-length, good-faith notarization.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Shantaram to explain his 1 April direct call with the buyer and the Rs 75,000 he received from the broker the day after the buyer's payment, given his statement that he doesn't know the buyer personally.

description: Rafiq's statement (WS-1) frames Vinod as a random 'regular walk-in customer', but the call record (CL-1) shows Vinod contacting Rafiq just 90 minutes after the burglary window closed, well before any normal shop-visit conversation would happen.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Rafiq why a 'regular walk-in customer' called him at 4:10am, 90 minutes after a nearby warehouse burglary, before any shop would normally be open.

description: Ismail's statement (WS-2) claims his call to Chandru was a 'routine payroll matter', but it directly precedes Chandru's calls to the two men who carried out the assault (CL-2, CL-3), and a witness (WS-1) directly attributes an instruction to Chandru right after that call.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Ismail what specifically was discussed in the 17 Jan 5:30pm call to Chandru, given it precedes by under an hour the calls that mobilized the two men who assaulted Hanumantha.

description: Somesh's statement (WS-1, given only after FIR 9009) claims his truck was used without his knowledge and he was asleep - but the exact same truck was flagged on the same toll camera at nearly the same hour a week later (CC-2), right after another Halappa-to-Somesh call (CL-2) matching the first night's pattern precisely, which is hard to square with a one-off unauthorized use.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Somesh how his truck ended up on the same toll camera at nearly the same hour a second time, one week after he says it was used without his knowledge, following another call from Halappa that matches the first night's pattern.

description: Priya's statement (WS-1) claims she is only a landlord with no involvement in the office's activity, but the shell company both victims paid into (TX-1, TX-2) pays out directly to her personal HDFC account (TX-3), and CCTV shows her entering the office alongside the agents (CC-1), not visiting as an occasional landlord would.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Priya to explain the Rs 88,000 transfer from the 'TechFix Solutions' shell account - the same account both victims paid into - to her personal HDFC account, given her statement that she has no involvement beyond leasing the space.

description: Kamala's recanted statement (WS-2) claims 'no one visited or spoke to me' since her first statement, but CCTV (CC-1) places the accused's brother entering her building that exact morning, less than an hour before she gave the recant - and a call from the accused to his brother (CL-1) precedes that visit.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Kamala directly about Nandish Iyengar's visit to her building at 9:20am on 4 March, less than an hour before her recanted statement, which contradicts her claim that no one visited her.

description: Vasant's statement (WS-1) frames this as routine bulk scrap buying with no questions asked, but the timing is too tight for that story - a call 30 minutes after the theft (CL-1), scooters delivered by hand rather than ridden in (CC-1, consistent with them being stolen and disabled/hidden), and same-day payment (TX-1, TX-2) to both men involved.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Vasant why he paid Sagar and Ganesh cash the same morning two scooters were pushed (not ridden) into his garage, 30 minutes after a call from Sagar right after the theft window.

description: Ravi's statement (WS-1) claims he never left the hall and doesn't know any of the accused, but a call record (CL-1) shows him contacting Altaf 90 minutes before the robbery with details matching what was stolen, and he received a payment from Altaf 3 days later (TX-1).
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Ravi to explain his 6:30pm call to Altaf Pathan, 90 minutes before the robbery, and the Rs 25,000 he received from him 3 days later, given his statement that he doesn't know any of the accused.

description: Clifton's statement (WS-1) frames himself purely as a fellow victim who recruited 'in good faith', but a call from Wilfred to him (CL-2) on 1 September - the exact day investors stopped getting answers - precedes the mass fund transfer out (TX-3) by 2 days, suggesting advance knowledge rather than innocence.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Clifton what Wilfred told him in the 1 September call, the same day investors stopped receiving responses and two days before Wilfred transferred Rs 42 lakh out of the country.

description: Deepak's statement (WS-1, given in the Ballari FIR) claims he never operated in Bengaluru, but the Bengaluru cash-out (TX-2) lands in the exact same account (xx7761) as the Ballari cash-out (TX-1), and a call from him to Anand (CL-3) is timed precisely with the Bengaluru withdrawals.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Deepak why cloned-card cash-outs from both Ballari and Bengaluru settle into the same account xx7761, given his statement that his activity was limited to Ballari.

description: Devaraj's statement (WS-1) claims he was on 'regular night duty as always' and noticed nothing, but a call from him to Manjappa the night before (CL-1) and a payment from Manjappa to him the day after the timber sale (TX-2) both point to prior coordination, not routine duty.
suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Devaraj about his 9pm call to Manjappa the night before the trees were felled, and the Rs 40,000 he received from him the day after the timber was sold, given his statement that it was a routine night with nothing unusual.

description: Both sides claim self-defense (WS-1 says Bharath's group struck first, WS-2 says Zaid's group struck first) - but wide-angle CCTV (CC-2) directly shows Bharath throwing the first visible strike, which contradicts WS-2's account but is worth weighing against the earlier coordination call on Bharath's side (CL-2, 2 hours before) versus the later, more reactive-looking call on Zaid's side (CL-1, 40 min before).
suggestedNextQuestion: Show Bharath the wide-angle CCTV timestamped 17:31 and ask him to reconcile it with his statement that Zaid's group struck first - and ask why his side's coordination call (2 hours prior) precedes Zaid's side's (40 min prior) by so much, if this was a reactive, unplanned encounter.
